VERDICT_FOR_THE_OPERATOR: You are right and we were wrong about the number, not about the fact: Hays County is not missing 30,000+ properties. An authority neither we nor Hays CAD control -- Hays CAD's own 2025 Annual Report, which states its property count 'based on the 2025 Comptroller's Audit Reports' -- puts the account count at 132,358 to 132,538 for 2025, which is within 2% of the 134,606 we ingested for 2026 and represents normal one-year growth, not a 21.8% collapse. The 172,116 number our program was comparing against was never a real Hays CAD roll count -- it was our own 2025 baseline after we grafted 116,421 non-CAD StratMap land-parcel rows onto it five weeks ago. That graft, not Hays CAD's appraisal roll, is where the appearance of a 30,000-property gap came from.

lessons: Hays CAD's own Annual Report is a genuinely useful independent cross-check for this program going forward: it publishes a 'Number of Accounts' figure and a Comptroller-audit-sourced category breakdown every year, in prose/PDF form, entirely outside the bulk-download pipeline this program ingests. Any future roll-size dispute for a Texas county should check for an equivalent CAD annual report before assuming our own store is the only measurement available -- most Texas CADs publish one (it is a common, sometimes statutorily-encouraged, transparency practice).

The Texas Comptroller's PTAD PVS site (comptroller.texas.gov/auto-data/PT2/PVS/) carries genuine per-category, per-ISD parcel counts but does not publish a rolled-up county grand total in one place, and its per-ISD summary tables appear to render client-side (visible via WebFetch's rendered read, absent from a raw curl fetch of the same URL). A future lane wanting to hand-verify a Comptroller total directly, rather than relying on a CAD's own citation of it, should expect to need a JS-capable fetch, not a plain HTTP GET.

Hays CAD's own official schema documentation for its Certified Export (an 'Orion Appraisal Export Layout.xlsx' file shipped inside the same zip as the data) is a small, directly authoritative reference for record-type codes -- reading it settled the R/P/M/N question in one file read, far cheaper than inferring meaning from proportions or guessing from the dispatch's own hypothesis (which, this lane found, had M and N reversed).
deadEnds: Attempting to hand-reconstruct the Comptroller's own grand total for Hays by summing all 7 ISD x ~12 category worksheets directly from comptroller.texas.gov -- the per-district Summary Worksheet tables did not appear in a raw curl fetch of the index page (likely client-side rendered), and pursuing this further was judged not worth the marginal confidence gain given the strength of the corroboration already in hand from Hays CAD's own Annual Report. Named as a limitation above rather than silently abandoned.
